subject: ACME: Post-demo recap + request for prompt set & edge cases
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Mills <sarah.mills@acme.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-06-15T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: ACME: Post-demo recap + request for prompt set & edge cases

Hi Sarah,

Thanks again for taking the time today — enjoyed walking through how Redwood can help reduce per-token cost while preserving generation quality for your customer support summaries and intent routing workloads. Quick recap and next steps from our side: 

- Key fit: your volume profile (short messages, many concurrent sessions) maps well to RW-chat-1.3 for chat-level quality and rw-instruct-large-v2-quant for cost-sensitive batch scoring.
- Observability: we'll add per-route cost/latency dashboards and a prompt-level regression monitor tied to your test prompts.

Action items I mentioned on the call: 
1) Could you share a representative set of prompts (both typical and edge cases)? Ideally ~200 rows covering common intents, low-frequency edge cases, and any examples containing structured tokens (order IDs, invoice numbers).
2) Please indicate redaction constraints (PII you cannot share, e.g., customer emails, full payment card numbers). We can provide a redaction template to run on your side.
3) Ben will run a short model-fit evaluation on samples you provide and share benchmark links and recommended model variants.

Attached is a short model-fit deck with our recommended config baseline and the metrics we'll evaluate (latency, top-1 accuracy vs. your labels, and hallucination checks). If you can get a CSV with the prompt + expected label/desired output by EOD next Wed (2026-06-24), we'll prioritize the eval.

Attachments: redwood_model-fit-deck.pdf (application/pdf)

Thanks — looping Ben and Logan to own the eval and data intake.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
From: Sarah Mills <sarah.mills@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: James Park <james.park@acme.com>
Date: 2026-06-16T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: ACME: Post-demo recap + request for prompt set & edge cases

Thanks Marissa — great demo yesterday. A few notes from our side: 

- We can share a first pass of prompts but we have strict PII rules. We will redact emails and full payment card numbers. We can provide tokenized order IDs (e.g., ORD-xxxx) and last-4 for cards.
- Two initial use cases: 1) triage/intent classification for support messages, 2) summary generation for billing disputes.

I attached a small sample file (acme_prompt_examples_v1.csv) to start. We can expand to the ~200 row target once we confirm redaction.

Question: will you be able to run the evals on staging with masked data or do you need the unredacted original for best results? Also — can you share the benchmark link and the recommended model variants for both accuracy and cost?

Regards,
Sarah Mills
Product Ops | Acme Corp
sarah.mills@acme.com

Date: 2026-06-16T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: ACME: Post-demo recap + request for prompt set & edge cases

Hi Sarah — thanks for the sample. Quick answers and a guidance pack attached.

Short answers: 
- Yes — redacted/masked data is fine for most of the fit/eval steps. For narrow failure-analysis (e.g., hallucinations tied to specific user names) we may ask for a short locked dataset accessible via your staging environment or via a secure transfer; we'll follow your security constraints.
- Recommended starting models: rw-chat-1.3 (best balance for conversational summarization), rw-instruct-large-v2-quant (good cost/quality tradeoff for batch scoring), and a quantized small variant rw-instruct-medium-quant for low-cost A/B routing. We will run all three for your sample and produce a per-model cost/latency/accuracy table.

Attached: prompt_collection_template.csv (CSV template for expected columns: prompt_id,prompt_text,expected_label,category,edge_case_flag)
Attached: redaction_guidelines.md (short checklist and regex suggestions for common PII types)

Next steps I propose:
1) Sarah: expand the CSV to ~200 rows, flag edge cases as mentioned.
2) Ben/Logan: run the initial eval on the three recommended variants and share the benchmark link + a short writeup on any quality regressions we see.
3) Marissa: follow up with procurement resources if we need an NDA/secure transfer for unredacted test sets.

Would you be available for a 30-minute sync Thurs morning (June 18) to review the initial results? I can send a calendar invite.

—Ben
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
From: Sarah Mills <sarah.mills@acme.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: James Park <james.park@acme.com>
Date: 2026-06-16T15:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: ACME: Post-demo recap + request for prompt set & edge cases

Ben — attaching a larger set (acme_prompt_set_v2.csv) with ~120 rows for now. Two edge cases to flag: 
1) Users who paste HTML snippets into support tickets (we see broken markup and embedded links) — please include an example row with raw HTML in the prompt_text.
2) Invoice/order numbers that are mixed alphanumeric (e.g., INV2026-AB12) — these sometimes confuse extractors.

On the redaction front: we will remove full emails and full card numbers. Order IDs can be left unchanged but we can mask customer emails. We are open to a secure staging transfer for unredacted samples if needed for deeper analysis, pending an NDA.

Questions: 
- Can you confirm whether Redwood's eval will run on our staging environment or do we need to upload samples to your secure bucket?
- What retention do you apply to samples used for model-fit/evals?

Thanks,
Sarah
